hypotheses.justification: `hk` follows from the other hypotheses: `hb0 : 0 ≤ b` and `hb : b < k` give `0 < k` (so do `hc0` and `hc`). To delete it, add `have hk : 0 < k := by omega` (or `lt_of_le_of_lt hb0 hb`) at the start of the proof. The rest of the proof, which uses `hk` only in `abs_of_pos hk`, then works unchanged. None of the other hypotheses can be dropped. Without `hb0`: take b = c - k with c = 0, so b - c = -k, `(-k) % k = 0`, and b ≠ c. Without `hb`: take b = c + k. The cases without `hc0` or `hc` are symmetric.
